answer: Each applicant receives one walnut shell, its ridges scanned and hashed to its key. At dawn the registry sends a tone; the holder plays it through the shell and files the resonance spectrum, and the next tone follows from that spectrum and the key, so tones chain. Between tones the shell makes a voyage by courier to a lab for a re-scan before the next tone opens. A replayed spectrum fails: no two shells share one ridge pattern. One shell costs $300 plus 19 tuning-hours; 5,000 fakes would need 5,000 shells, $1.5 million and 95,000 hours, and no orchard grows two shells with the same ridges.
